decision_conditions: All tree works will be carried out in accordance with British Standard 3998: 2010 Tree work. Recommendations. In order to carry out the tree works to BS 3998:2010 there will be only the removal of secondary and tertiary branches, no primary branches. All finalpruning cuts on the branches will not exceed a third of the diameter of the main stem of the tree when measured at 1.5 meters above ground level. Reason: To ensure that the works are carried out in accordance with good arboricultural practice.

This decision notice for Tree Works is only valid for 2 years from the date of this decision or until the work is completed, whichever is the sooner. Reason: In order to ensure that the work is carried out whilst still appropriate and in accordance with the time period within the legislation and regulations.

The council considers that there is insufficient technical justification to grant consent for the removal of the Yew tree, which continues to makes a positive, contribution to the local landscape.The submitted arboricultural report fails to substantiate the Applicants concerns over subsidence damage. The observed vertical cracking on the building elevation is characteristic of thermal movement or render drying rather than the diagonal fracturing typical of clay-shrinkage subsidence. Additionally, the localised lifting of adjacent paving is standard surface root development, which can be managed through a small scale repair and/or removing a small section of block paving around the stem. The presence of yew berries is a natural feature of the species and does not warrant felling a protected tree.The council therefore refuses consent to fell T1. However, as a split decision, the council approves a proportionate crown reduction to manage the canopy size appropriately while preserving the tree's health and landscape value.
